questions.question: What is the supreme law of the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The 1987 Constitution is the fundamental and supreme law of the land. All other laws must conform to it. It was ratified on February 2, 1987.

questions.question: How many branches of government does the Philippines have?
questions.explanation: The Philippine government has three co-equal branches: Executive (President), Legislative (Congress), and Judiciary (Supreme Court). This follows the principle of separation of powers.
questions.source: 1987 Philippine Constitution — Article VI, VII, VIII

questions.question: What is the term of office of the President of the Philippines?
questions.explanation: Under the 1987 Constitution, the President serves a single term of 6 years without re-election. The Vice President serves the same term but may be re-elected for one additional term.

questions.question: Who has the power to declare martial law in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The President may declare martial law in case of invasion or rebellion when public safety requires it. However, Congress may revoke it, and the Supreme Court may review its constitutionality.

questions.question: What is the minimum age requirement to become President of the Philippines?
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution states that the President must be at least 40 years of age on the day of the election, a natural-born citizen, and a resident of the Philippines for at least 10 years.

questions.question: Which branch of government has the power to impeach the President?
questions.explanation: The House of Representatives has the exclusive power to initiate impeachment cases. The Senate has the sole power to try and decide impeachment cases. It's a two-step process involving both chambers.

questions.question: The Philippine Constitution guarantees the right to information on matters of:
questions.explanation: Article III, Section 7 of the Bill of Rights guarantees the right of the people to information on matters of public concern. This promotes transparency and accountability in government.

questions.question: According to the Constitution, the State shall protect and promote the right of the people to a balanced and healthful:
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 16 declares that 'The State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.'

questions.question: How many senators comprise the Philippine Senate?
questions.explanation: The Senate is composed of 24 senators elected at large by qualified Filipino voters. They serve a term of 6 years and may not serve more than two consecutive terms.

questions.question: Under the 1987 Constitution, who is the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Philippines?
options: Chief of Staff of the AFP
questions.explanation: Article VII, Section 18 states: 'The President shall be the Commander-in-Chief of all armed forces of the Philippines.' The President holds supreme military authority.

questions.question: RA 6713 is also known as:
options: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
questions.correctAnswer: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees
questions.explanation: Republic Act No. 6713, enacted in 1989, establishes a code of conduct and ethical standards for public officials and employees to uphold public interest over personal interest.
questions.source: RA 6713 — Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards

questions.question: Under RA 6713, public officials and employees must always uphold what over personal interest?
questions.explanation: Section 4(a) of RA 6713 states that public officials shall always uphold the public interest over and above personal interest. This is a fundamental ethical principle in public service.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the eight norms of conduct under RA 6713?
questions.explanation: RA 6713 lists eight norms of conduct: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, and simple living.

questions.question: Under RA 6713, public officials are prohibited from accepting gifts valued above what amount?
options: The law prohibits accepting any gift in connection with official duties
questions.correctAnswer: The law prohibits accepting any gift in connection with official duties
questions.explanation: RA 6713 prohibits public officials from soliciting or accepting, directly or indirectly, any gift, gratuity, favor, entertainment, loan, or anything of monetary value in the course of their official duties.

questions.question: According to RA 6713, what must public officials file annually?
options: Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN)
questions.correctAnswer: Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN)
questions.explanation: Section 8 of RA 6713 requires all public officials and employees to file under oath their SALN and a disclosure of business interests and financial connections annually.

questions.question: RA 9003 is also known as the:
questions.explanation: Republic Act No. 9003, enacted in 2001, provides the legal framework for systematic, comprehensive, and ecological solid waste management in the Philippines.
questions.source: RA 9003 — Ecological Solid Waste Management Act

questions.question: RA 8749 is known as the Philippine:
questions.explanation: Republic Act No. 8749, or the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999, provides for a comprehensive air quality management policy and program to achieve and maintain healthy air.

questions.question: RA 9275, the Philippine Clean Water Act, aims to protect:
questions.explanation: RA 9275 or the Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004 provides comprehensive water quality management to protect, preserve, and revive the quality of Philippine fresh, brackish, and marine waters.

questions.question: What does the '3R' principle in solid waste management stand for?
questions.explanation: RA 9003 promotes the 3Rs: Reduce (minimize waste generation), Reuse (use items repeatedly), and Recycle (process waste into new products). These form the foundation of ecological waste management.
questions.source: RA 9003 — Ecological Solid Waste Management Act

questions.question: Under RA 8749, what are the two major types of air pollutants?
questions.explanation: Primary pollutants are emitted directly from sources (e.g., carbon monoxide). Secondary pollutants form when primary pollutants react in the atmosphere (e.g., ground-level ozone). The Clean Air Act regulates both types.

questions.question: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) was adopted by the United Nations in:
questions.explanation: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly on December 10, 1948. This date is now celebrated annually as International Human Rights Day.

questions.question: Which article of the Philippine Constitution contains the Bill of Rights?
questions.explanation: Article III of the 1987 Philippine Constitution enumerates the Bill of Rights, which guarantees fundamental civil and political rights to all persons in the Philippines.

questions.question: What right is protected by the writ of habeas corpus?
questions.explanation: A writ of habeas corpus is a court order demanding that a person in custody be brought before the court to determine if the detention is lawful. It protects against arbitrary imprisonment.

questions.question: The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) in the Philippines was created by:
questions.explanation: Article XIII, Section 17 of the 1987 Constitution created the Commission on Human Rights as an independent office to investigate human rights violations involving civil and political rights.

questions.question: The Philippines is what type of government?
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution states: 'The Philippines is a democratic and republican State. Sovereignty resides in the people and all government authority emanates from them.'

questions.question: What is the highest court in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is the highest judicial body in the Philippines, composed of a Chief Justice and 14 Associate Justices. It is the court of last resort for all cases.

questions.question: How many justices comprise the Supreme Court of the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court is composed of 1 Chief Justice and 14 Associate Justices, totaling 15 members. They serve until age 70 or until they become incapacitated.

questions.question: What is the Sandiganbayan?
options: A trial court for criminal cases
A special court that tries graft and corruption cases against public officials
An appellate court for civil cases
questions.correctAnswer: A special court that tries graft and corruption cases against public officials
questions.explanation: The Sandiganbayan is a special appellate collegial court that has jurisdiction over criminal and civil cases involving graft and corrupt practices committed by public officers and employees.

questions.question: The Civil Service Commission (CSC) is responsible for:
options: Overseeing the civil service and government employees
questions.correctAnswer: Overseeing the civil service and government employees
questions.explanation: The CSC is the central personnel agency of the Philippine government, responsible for establishing a career service and promoting morale, efficiency, integrity, and responsiveness in the civil service.

questions.question: Under the Constitution, appointments in the civil service shall be made based on:
questions.explanation: Article IX-B, Section 2(2) of the Constitution states: 'Appointments in the civil service shall be made only according to merit and fitness to be determined, as far as practicable, by competitive examination.'

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT within the coverage of the Civil Service?
options: Government-owned and controlled corporations (GOCCs) with original charters
All branches of government including constitutional commissions
questions.explanation: The civil service covers all branches and agencies of government, including GOCCs with original charters. Private companies, even those with government contracts, are not part of the civil service.

questions.question: What do the three stars on the Philippine flag represent?
options: The three original provinces that revolted against Spain
questions.explanation: The three stars represent the three main geographical island groups of the Philippines: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
questions.source: Republic Act 8491 — Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines

questions.question: What do the eight rays of the sun on the Philippine flag represent?
options: Eight provinces that first revolted against Spain
questions.correctAnswer: Eight provinces that first revolted against Spain
questions.explanation: The eight rays represent the eight provinces that were placed under martial law by the Spanish colonial government for revolting: Manila, Cavite, Bulacan, Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, Tarlac, Laguna, and Batangas.
questions.source: Republic Act 8491 — Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines

questions.question: Who composed the Philippine national anthem?
questions.explanation: Julian Felipe composed the music of the Philippine national anthem 'Lupang Hinirang' in 1898. The lyrics were written by Jose Palma in 1899, originally as a poem titled 'Filipinas.'
questions.source: Republic Act 8491 — Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines

questions.question: RA 9485, also known as the Anti-Red Tape Act, aims to:
options: Reduce bureaucratic red tape and improve efficiency in government service delivery
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce bureaucratic red tape and improve efficiency in government service delivery
questions.explanation: RA 9485 (Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007), now amended by RA 11032 (Ease of Doing Business Act), requires government agencies to process transactions within specified timeframes to reduce bureaucratic delays.
questions.source: RA 11032 — Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act

questions.question: RA 6713 requires public officials to perform their duties with:
options: Highest degree of excellence, professionalism, intelligence, and skill
questions.correctAnswer: Highest degree of excellence, professionalism, intelligence, and skill
questions.explanation: Section 4(b) of RA 6713 mandates that public officials shall perform and discharge their duties with the highest degree of excellence, professionalism, intelligence, and skill.

questions.question: The principle that government funds must be spent only for public purposes is called:
questions.explanation: The public purpose doctrine holds that government may only use public funds for public purposes. This prevents the use of taxpayer money for private benefit and is a fundamental principle in public finance.

questions.question: The constitutional right against self-incrimination means:
options: A person can refuse to testify in any proceeding
A person cannot be compelled to testify against himself in a criminal case
A person cannot be arrested without a warrant
A person has the right to remain silent only during trial
questions.correctAnswer: A person cannot be compelled to testify against himself in a criminal case
questions.explanation: Article III, Section 17 of the Constitution states: 'No person shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.' This right applies specifically in criminal proceedings.

questions.question: PD 1151 requires government agencies to prepare what document for projects affecting the environment?
questions.explanation: Presidential Decree 1151 (Philippine Environmental Policy) requires all government agencies to prepare an Environmental Impact Statement for any action that may significantly affect the quality of the environment.

questions.question: Which government agency is primarily responsible for disaster response in the Philippines?
options: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC)
Department of Social Welfare and Development
questions.correctAnswer: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC)
questions.explanation: The NDRRMC, created under RA 10121, is the primary government agency responsible for disaster preparedness, response, and rehabilitation. It is headed by the Secretary of National Defense.
questions.source: RA 10121 — Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act

questions.question: RA 10931, the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act, provides:
options: Free tuition in state universities and colleges (SUCs)
questions.correctAnswer: Free tuition in state universities and colleges (SUCs)
questions.explanation: RA 10931, enacted in 2017, provides free tuition and other school fees for students enrolled in SUCs, local universities and colleges (LUCs), and state-run technical-vocational institutions.
questions.source: RA 10931 — Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act

questions.question: The 4Ps (Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program) is a government program that provides:
options: Conditional cash grants to poor households for health, nutrition, and education
questions.correctAnswer: Conditional cash grants to poor households for health, nutrition, and education
questions.explanation: The 4Ps is a poverty reduction strategy that provides conditional cash transfers to extremely poor households to improve health, nutrition, and education of children aged 0-18.
questions.source: RA 11310 — Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program Act

questions.question: Which constitutional commission is responsible for auditing all government funds?
questions.explanation: The Commission on Audit is an independent constitutional commission that examines, audits, and settles all accounts pertaining to government revenue, expenditures, and property use.

questions.question: The local government units in the Philippines include:
questions.explanation: Under the Local Government Code (RA 7160), the territorial and political subdivisions of the Philippines are provinces, cities, municipalities, and barangays. Regions are administrative groupings, not separate LGUs.

questions.question: According to the Constitution, the State shall promote a just and dynamic social order that will ensure the prosperity and independence of the nation through policies that provide:
options: Adequate social services, full employment, a rising standard of living, and an improved quality of life for all
questions.correctAnswer: Adequate social services, full employment, a rising standard of living, and an improved quality of life for all
questions.explanation: Article II, Section 9 declares this as a state policy. The Constitution mandates the State to promote social justice and ensure the welfare of all Filipinos.

questions.question: Under RA 6713, how long must a public official wait before accepting employment in a private enterprise that had official business with their former office?
questions.explanation: Section 9(b) of RA 6713 prohibits public officials, for one year after resignation or separation from service, from accepting employment in any private enterprise regulated or having official transactions with their former office.

questions.question: What does the constitutional right to 'equal protection of the laws' mean?
options: Everyone must be treated exactly the same in all situations
Persons similarly situated should be treated alike under the law
The government cannot pass any laws
questions.correctAnswer: Persons similarly situated should be treated alike under the law
questions.explanation: Equal protection means that all persons or things similarly situated should be treated alike, both as to rights conferred and responsibilities imposed. It allows reasonable classification but prohibits arbitrary discrimination.

questions.question: Which Philippine law mandates the establishment of a national identification system?
questions.explanation: RA 11055, or the Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) Act, established a single national identification system for all citizens and resident aliens. It is implemented by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA).

questions.question: The legislative power in the Philippines is vested in:
questions.explanation: Article VI, Section 1 states: 'The legislative power shall be vested in the Congress of the Philippines which shall consist of a Senate and a House of Representatives.' Congress makes, amends, and repeals laws.
